#852. Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich

Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich.

That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett.

Harry Winks was the last academy graduate to score on his debut more than a decade ago – a feat that Kane also achieved two years earlier against Sunderland. Yet after Spurs decided to allow the England Under-21s striker Will Lankshear to join Middlesbrough in the summer, there was no chance that Williams-Barnett would be allowed to follow him out of the door. He became the 900th player ever to represent Spurs when he made his debut last year and the teenager left the field here to a standing ovation that he will never forget.

“I told him to play like he plays in the park with his friends, with the same freedom,” said De Zerbi. “And to play and to work hard without the ball, like [Ousmane] Dembélé, like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal. Luca is a special player. I’m not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think. He’s very young but at same time he’s very mature. He is older than his age.”

Asked whether his protege has the potential to be compared to the Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal, De Zerbi added: “Yes, I think so. One of the best things in my career I’ve seen today on the bus to the stadium. He was watching [clips] on YouTube of Ronaldinho, Hazard. I think he’s a special guy, because if one hour before you are debuting in the Premier League, you are watching Ronaldinho, Hazard, Neymar, all these types of talent. Having the qualities is one thing but he has the passion for football, too.”

After a promising start to the campaign, Ipswich’s momentum has stalled – they have now gone five games without a victory. But Gary O’Neil, who has already seen 16-year-old Max Dowman score twice for Arsenal against his side in the Carabao Cup, acknowledged that they had been second best throughout. “You need things to be perfect when we come to a place like this and we didn’t make things easy for ourselves,” he said.

De Zerbi dropped a huge hint that Williams-Barnett could be handed his opportunity to start after two impressive cameos against Crystal Palace and Leeds. “Maybe, maybe,” he said on Friday. It turned out that the decision was actually taken last week, although the absence of Sandro Tonali due to illness forced Spurs into a reshuffle in midfield as Mateus Fernandes was handed the holding role.

Solanke has struggled to fill the void left by Kane since joining from Bournemouth in 2024 but looked in determined mood and he was inches wide with a swivel and shot from inside the area. A driving run from Williams-Barnett had the home supporters off their feet, with Solanke again going close from the resulting corner. It then needed a timely block from the teenager to stop Ipswich breaking downfield.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

His big moment arrived less than 60 seconds later. Porro’s ball to the back post should have been dealt with by Abdoul Ouattara, only for a moment’s hesitation to allow Williams-Barnett to muscle in front of him and apply the finish with his knee. “He’s one of our own,” sang the Tottenham fans in delight.

Mohammed Kudus was unfortunate to see his superb effort from a free-kick cannon off the inside of the post and away to safety. Williams-Barnett will be disappointed not to have scored his second when he miskicked inside the six-yard box with the goal gaping. James Maddison was then denied by a brilliant save from Christian Walton and Williams-Barnett left the field at half-time looking very pleased with himself as he waved to his family in the crowd.

His smile grew even broader after Darnell Furlong was left bamboozled by a direct run down the left flank before the youngster delivered the ball on a plate for Solanke to score his first goal here since March. The defeat could have been worse for Ipswich had it not been for Walton, and O’Neil will know they are in danger of being sucked into trouble if this winless run continues. There are no such concerns for Tottenham these days. Thanks to Williams-Barnett, their future looks much brighter than a few weeks ago.

#851. Champion’s corner: KC Current win first NWSL Championship with 2-1 stunner over Spirit

Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick

Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time

Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final

Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report

It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.

Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute Olimpico from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.

The Spirit, heartbroken at the final whistle, have now lost three consecutive NWSL Championships.

“Obviously this one hates way worse than any of the other ones,” forward Trinity Rodman said afterward. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment — it is too fresh.”

DiBernardo’s goal was stunning, a driven, bent corner kick played to the far post that eluded Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver, her defenders and Current forward Haley Hopkins, potentially DiBernardo’s intended target. The Spirit’s players and fans alike pleaded with center referee Joshua Encarnación, suggesting he examine the play on VAR for obstruction, as MacIver had potentially been screened. The review never came.

Whether played directly on goal intentionally or otherwise, the effort will go down as one of the most memorable in NWSL Championship history. At 34, DiBernardo becomes the oldest player in league history to score in a final, and was later named the match’s MVP.

“I’ve been to the game a few times and haven’t won, but this one just felt a little lighter,” said DiBernardo, who gave birth to Charlie, her first child, in January and took time off before returning to the Current in March. “I think just having Charlie, it just brings a different perspective on life. I knew the game was big and it was a big moment, but just kinda having her, just spending the day with her, it just felt really special.”

The game’s early phases were forgettable save for one incident which would go on to affect the remainder of the match: a bruising, high-speed tackle on Rodman by Current defender Laney Rouse in the fifth minute. The challenge sent Rodman flying and appeared to injure her left elbow; the Spirit forward, nearing tears, spent much of the first half in visible pain and seemingly never fully recovered. Rouse was not cautioned for the challenge.

“[It helped set the tone] in the sense that it hurt really bad, yes,” Rodman said. “As a team, you always want to put the first hit in. You’re taught to do that. Credit to them. I wish I was the one who put her on the ground. They did a really good job at setting the tone and controlling the first half.”

It was far from the game’s only physical moment. Neither team managed to settle into any meaningful rhythm during an opening 45 that felt at times more like a title fight than a title match. Encarnación, involved in his first NWSL final, called a very tight match and the near-constant stoppages in play were the defining characteristic of a sometimes ugly opening phase. In many ways it was not entirely his fault: the message-sending start from KC and the Spirit’s subsequent response often compelled him to act. The 19 combined first-half fouls between both sides were the most in any half of any NWSL title match in league history.

“It felt like we couldn’t play more than two minutes without a whistle,” Rodman said. “We were fouling, they were true calls for sure — but I think you lose control of the game really quickly that way ... It definitely messed with our rhythm a little bit.”

Paradoxically, though, the match was won with speed. Deep into second-half stoppage time, the Current found their eventual match-winner on a breakaway. After doggedly winning back possession after a Spirit free kick late on, Kansas City forward Debinha streaked upfield from just beyond the center stripe, looking off a wide-open Temwa Chawinga and rounding MacIver who looked on hopelessly as the Brazilian slotted it home.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Moments later, Rodman – somehow still in the match after not only the early challenge but a later high-speed collision with Current goalkeeper Lorena – pulled one back for the Spirit. Falling away from goal 10 yards out, Rodman got her head on the end of a Tara Rudd cross, placing it perfectly over Lorena’s outstretched arms and into the far-side netting. The ensuing five minutes – the game ended in the 102nd – were chaotic but the Spirit couldn’t quite find the equalizer.

After a slow start, the Current were well-managed by former Major League Soccer and US national team member Chris Armas. Armas was widely considered a controversial selection at the time of his appointment but proceeded to lead the club to their first championship in his first season, doing so by beating Gotham FC and now the Spirit, two sides picked by many as potential league-winners.

“I think from the front to the back we made it a point that every person on this team defends and if somebody is going to make a mistake the other person is going to have their back,” Current defender Izzy Rodriguez said. “We try and turn every 1v1 situation into a 1v2 for us, and I think that showed up today. We were winning our duels and second balls and those are things that win games.”

For the Spirit, the loss is devastating. They become the first American professional club – men’s or women’s – to lose three consecutive finals since the New England Revolution of Major League Soccer, who did so in the mid 2000s. In their five Championship appearances, the Spirit have won just one time, in 2021.

#850. Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments

Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy

Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better".

Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction".

Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had".

The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned, external the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested, external the deal may need to be renegotiated.

"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement., external

"In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better."

Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness

Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala?

Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September.

He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist.

"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

"Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months".

#848. Hirst key for Stoke, injuries derail Millwall - Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways

After the last international break of the year, Final Score pundit and former Swindon Town, Luton Town and Northampton Town striker selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

Stoke City are the Championship's form team, having taken 32 points from the last 39, but can they stay the distance in the promotion race?

Parkin: "I think everyone, probably me included, is really optimistic about their chances of this being the season they get it right.

"We're a fair chunk into the season now and I thought today's result was really important because I believe this was their first win over anyone in the top eight. It felt like a bit of a statement win because Birmingham, apart from their defeat at Cardiff, have been really competitive in more or less every game.

"They've been able to just come out the right side of the scoreline and they've had to rely on their goalkeeper [Viktor] Johansson, who I think is one of the top goalkeepers at this level.

"I think there was an early shift in formation, going to a back three in the early part of the campaign, and I think that's proved quite important. They're keeping clean sheets and they've got a goalscorer in George Hirst.

"I read a lot about Stoke City fans saying they're still probably short on forwards who are going to get them the goals. I know that [Jack] McGlynn has chipped in with a really impressive number from midfield, but for Hirst to get that big winning goal, that will have done his confidence the world of good.

"He's been promoted previously with Ipswich and there's no reason why he can't be Stoke's main man up front."

Millwall have slumped to 16th after fighting for promotion in the last few seasons and they have lost five of their last seven league games.

Parkin: "They've had to deal with a horrendous injury crisis. It was at a level that I was struggling to think of a comparable club in the early part of the season. They were just having players go down week after week.

"There was one game in particular I covered against Wrexham and they had the walking wounded (out there), so I think they're still recovering from that.

"They've got some of the main players in [Casper] De Norre back fit now and available, but I think [Josh] Coburn was unavailable again today, and [Mihailo] Ivanovic is just making his way back - I would say they are three of their more important players.

"Take away [Jake] Cooper at the back, who's been a mainstay for a number of years, and I think that trio I've just mentioned are so fundamental to their chances this season.

"They're still playing catch up to a degree, but Alex Neil has not pulled any punches in some of his interviews and he'll be disappointed.

"On the flip side of that, QPR are in a really good place at the moment, and are a much tougher proposition than maybe they would have been over the last couple of seasons.

"I think Millwall will improve over time. I don't see them emulating what they did last season, but I think they can be optimistic they can get some better results once everyone's back available."

Lincoln City management duo Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw

Lincoln City are finding life in the Championship tough after romping to the League One title last season and they have lost seven of their last nine league games.

Parkin: "It's been a downward spiral and the home form's a bit of an issue. They just have the one win over Burnley there - and Burnley were in dire straits when they came.

"They've lost four in a row so that will be a little bit of a concern because they found a formula on the road in the early part of the season. But, yeah, you've got to do better in your home form.

"I still trust they're going to be competitive and the majority of that squad, Jack Moylan apart, is still there from last season. You don't get over 100 points and then lose everything.

"That's always going to count for something when you've got the nucleus of that squad still together, even if it is in a higher division. So I think the spirit will remain amongst that group, despite the recent defeats.

"They've got to start taking points off the better teams in the division as well. All their victories have come against teams who are in the lower part of the table, like Preston and Burnley.

"They won at Bolton and at Bristol City, so they're not really mixing it with the teams in the top half of the table at the moment.

"But I think the bottom line is the management duo would have absolutely taken being five points above 22nd at this stage of the season, so they've given themselves a good opportunity to stay in the division."

Barnsley are four points from safety at the bottom of League One after Friday's defeat by Sheffield Wednesday in the South Yorkshire derby and are on course for a first return to the fourth tier since 1979.

Parkin: "I think on last night's evidence, they're a better team than the league table suggests. That's an absolute certainty in my mind.

"My one concern is where are the goals going to come from? For all their dangerous play, which is incredibly aggressive and energetic, with and without the ball, where are the goals?

"They throw caution to the wind and there's a real energy and youth about the side, which I actually really admired in defeat.

"It's just translating all that into goals and that was obviously one part of it against Wednesday, and giving away bad goals - they've conceded the most set pieces now in the division.

"They conceded in that manner again, and because they play such a high line, they (also) get exposed by teams on the counter. Maybe that's a little bit of naivety. Maybe that's a little bit lack of experience, which they can go some way to mending in January when the transfer window opens.

"But they may be adrift at the bottom if they don't turn things around soon. In short, I think they're a better team than a relegated team. But the most important thing in football, as we know, is putting the ball in the back of the net and that clearly is a problem for them at the moment."

Crawley Town's Dylan Morgan celebrates scoring against Cheltenham Town

Crawley Town boosted their chances of staying in the EFL when they recorded their first home league win of the season over Fleetwood Town and they have generated some momentum in their last few matches.

Parkin: "Former Leeds and Sheffield United manager Kevin Blackwell is in charge now till the end of the season. I was injured for the majority of his spell at Luton Town when he was my manager, but I'm kind of well versed in his methods and he will make them really hard to beat.

"That's always the first thing you want when you take over a struggling side, you need to stop shipping goals. You need to get them organised. You need to work on set-pieces and be a threat on that front. He will do all those things.

"I think the three results in the league, two wins and a draw, have showed you that his methods have already come to fruition. His approach will be very different to probably what the players were being asked to do under Scott Lindsey.

"It'll be a different kind of football. They'll play long at times, they'll want to play in the opposition's half. I think in terms of a plan to get survival, he could very well be the man to supply that.

"They've chosen him after he was initially brought in as interim manager because the performances have improved across the last few weeks, despite the embarrassment of the FA Cup defeat to Wimborne.

"He's made them competitive very quickly and I think a lot of teams are going to be in for a real game when they face them."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's David Anderson

#847. Lionel Messi at center of red-card controversy as Inter Miami face early MLS playoff exit

Messi booked for throwing ball into opponent’s face

Columbus coach insists Argentine deserved red card

Defending champions thrashed 3-0 in series opener

Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after throwing a ball into an opponent’s face as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he hurled a throw-in into the face of Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia, with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.

Messi and Tapia were both shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards that the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.

“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said at a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.”

Chapman later defended his decision to show Messi only a yellow card.

“The force used was negligible and the offense did not reach the level of violent conduct,” Chapman told a pool reporter.

Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were trailing 1-0 after an early penalty from the Chile international Tapia.

The reigning MLS champions went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Taha Habroune doubling Columbus’s lead shortly after half-time before Tapia added his second at Miami’s Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh-seeded Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in Game 2 of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

“It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them,” Miami coach Kily González said afterwards.

“We didn’t produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don’t win, we’re out.

“There’s no better challenge for us as a team than this. It’s a test of character, and I know my team has that character.”

Joaquín Valiente scored twice in the space of two minutes as FC Dallas beat the Portland Timbers 3-0 in the opening game of their best-of-three Western Conference first-round series.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder broke the deadlock in the 53rd minute, volleying home a rebound after Daniel Job’s shot was parried by Portland goalkeeper James Pantemis.

Valiente doubled the lead two minutes later, timing his run to meet another pass from Job before redirecting the ball between Pantemis’s legs.

Samuel Sarver completed the scoring in the fourth minute of stoppage time, finishing a cross from Logan Farrington on the counterattack.

Dallas goalkeeper Daniel de Sousa Britto, known simply as Daniel, made four saves, while Pantemis finished with five for Portland.

The Timbers also lost Ariel Lassiter to an apparent injury in the 33rd minute.

Second-seeded Dallas can advance to the Western Conference semi-finals with a victory in Portland next Saturday.

Teenager Peyton Miller scored one goal and helped create another as the New England Revolution beat the Philadelphia Union 2-0 in the opening game of their Eastern Conference first-round series.

The 19-year-old Miller became the fifth-youngest goalscorer in MLS Cup playoffs history when he volleyed home a cross from Jack Harrison in the 73rd minute, his effort bouncing off the crossbar and into the net.

New England had taken the lead in the 10th minute when Miller’s shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel for an own goal.

Harrison, who came on as a substitute in the 62nd minute, was making his first appearance since 9 September after missing more than two months with a quadriceps injury.

Philadelphia nearly equalized in the 37th minute when Cavan Sullivan turned and fired a shot from outside the penalty area that struck the left post.

The Union fielded the youngest starting lineup in MLS Cup playoffs history, with an average age of 23 years and 207 days, breaking the record set by the New York Red Bulls in 2022.

Matt Turner made two saves to preserve the shutout for New England, who can advance to the Eastern Conference semi-finals with a victory in Philadelphia next Saturday.

#846. What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?

The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

The two-day talks between delegations from Ukraine, the US and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11 ended without a ceasefire agreement.

The main outcome was an agreement on a prisoner exchange.

"We have agreed on the largest humanitarian release of prisoners, and tomorrow we will finalize the numbers," Jared Kushner announced after the talks. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Moscow on Thursday, where they are due to meet President Vladimir Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier suggested an exchange of "1,000 for 1,000" prisoners, or "1,500 for 1,500." Russia said a large-scale prisoner exchange with Ukraine could take place within the next two to three weeks.

Following the meetings, Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram that the parties had discussed security guarantees and that "the first step should be ending this war and ensuring Ukraine's security." He also stressed that Europe should be involved "at every stage of genuine diplomacy."

Experts interviewed by DW agree that the main outcome of the talks is humanitarian.

"The agreement on a prisoner exchange is already a major step forward," says Artjom Bronzhukov of the Ukrainian think tank Polityka.

Pavlo Lakiychuk of the Ukrainian Center for Global Studies Strategy XXI also viewed it as a "very tangible result." He told DW that "getting our people back is already a major success. That is why it is worth continuing."

A real breakthrough, he added, would be the release of civilian detainees from territories occupied since 2014, particularly people from Crimea, who have been held in Russian prisons for years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Davyd Arakhamia, head of the ruling Servant of the People parliamentary faction and Ukraine's representative at the talks in Abu Dhabi, gave a positive assessment of the trilateral talks with the US and Russia, expressing hope that an agreement could be reached by the end of the year.

"I think the Russians came with extremely strict instructions, and it was difficult to ease the tone of the discussion. But the way the US representatives structured the talks with a view to the postwar situation in both countries opened up a dialogue, in my opinion, and allowed us to work together more productively," Arakhamia said at a joint press conference with US and Ukrainian representatives following the talks.

Iuliia Osmolovska of the Kyiv office of the international think tank GLOBSEC cautions against reading too much into the positive assessments of the talks from Washington and Kyiv.

"Diplomats taking part in negotiations will never say that everything went badly and that they have no expectations. Even when no results are achieved, they will still emphasize that the talks were constructive," she said. "For anyone familiar with diplomatic language, these are simply standard phrases."

Osmolovska points to a joint assessment by 71 Ukrainian security and defense experts published by GLOBSEC in the summer. According to the assessment, the chances of a peace agreement or at least a ceasefire being reached this year or next stand at just 19%.

She blames this on the fact that neither side is "ready" for genuine negotiations. Russia, in particular, has yet to accept that its objectives cannot be achieved by military means. "What we are seeing now is more of a farce, an attempt by all sides to put a brave face on things and create the impression that something is moving forward," Osmolovska said.

Artjom Bronzhukov sees the talks as a way for Moscow to buy time.

"The visits by the Russian delegation, particularly under the leadership of Vladimir Medinsky, are nothing more than an attempt to stall and sell empty promises to the US administration in the form of grand agreements, in order to continue receiving so-called gestures of goodwill from Washington, such as the lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel," the political scientist says.

Ahead of the talks, several Western media outlets reported on new US proposals concerning disputed territories. The Economist, for example, reported on a proposal to redraw the administrative boundaries of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions. However, a member of the Ukrainian delegation stressed that there had "never been any discussion of concessions on territories occupied by Russia."

Washington made no official comment on the reports.

Kyrylo Budanov, a member of the negotiating delegation and head of the Ukrainian president's office, declined to say whether Russia had used the talks to demand that Ukrainian troops withdraw from the Donbas. Asked by journalists whether Moscow was still insisting that Ukraine pull out of the region, Budanov said the content of the negotiations would remain confidential until an agreement was reached.

"The issues discussed in the talks are matters for negotiation. The only thing that matters is the outcome. Once we achieve it, it will be made public," Budanov said.

The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, took a different tone, declaring that "every inch of our land will be returned to Russia one way or another." He was responding to reports in European media that Ukraine was rejecting territorial concessions.

In addition to the Crimean Peninsula, annexed in 2014, Russian President Vladimir Putin claims the four Ukrainian regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson in their entirety as Russian territory, even though Russia does not have full military control over them.

"Putin is not fighting over villages and ruined cowsheds in the Donbas. He is fighting for geopolitical influence and trying to exploit the collapse of the old world order," says Artjom Bronzhukov.

The expert from the Polityka think tank recalls that Ukraine was already asked in early 2026 to withdraw its troops from the part of the Donbas it controls and turn the area into a free economic zone. Such a zone "would very quickly become a Russian-controlled area," he warns.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Pavlo Lakiychuk questions the idea of changing administrative boundaries.

"Why would Putin stop there?" asks the expert from the Strategy XXI center. In his view, US negotiators are seeking to extract unilateral concessions from Ukraine "step by step" without demanding anything in return from Russia.

Iuliia Osmolovska describes the proposal as "very original," but says it would pose risks for Ukraine's leadership. Even if the Ukrainian delegation agreed to it, which Osmolovska doubts, the decision would have to be explained to the public, which, she says, is not ready to accept it.

The GLOBSEC expert points out that, following the last harsh winter, marked by shortages of electricity and heating, only 5% of Ukrainians were willing to make concessions to Russia in exchange for an end to attacks on the energy sector.

Following the meeting between Jared Kushner, US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin in Moscow, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he wants to "coordinate positions with the Americans once again." No further trilateral meetings have been announced so far.

Iuliia Osmolovska believes the parties will sooner or later have to admit that the negotiations have reached a dead end. She expects each side to return to military action.

Pavlo Lakiychuk, by contrast, believes the talks should continue, if only to secure the return of prisoners. He is also convinced that Europeans "will always be there," because the issue is not just the Russian-Ukrainian war but the security of the entire continent.

This article was originally published in Ukrainian.

#845. Nine wins in a row - Bournemouth & Evanilson continue to make history

Evanilson strikes again as Bournemouth see off Forest

"We have to stick together and face reality."

That is how Bournemouth manager Marco Rose responded after his side had dropped into the Premier League relegation zone with a 5-1 defeat by Chelsea.

Six weeks on, it is an entirely different story.

The Cherries are up to fourth in the top flight, having clinched a club record ninth successive win in all competitions - with five in the league.

It is a far cry from that thumping defeat at Stamford Bridge, which left Rose without a victory in his first six Premier League matches in charge.

Bournemouth earned just three points from those six games (draws against Everton, Newcastle and Brentford - when the Cherries squandered winning positions) and fans may have been fearing the worst.

From the outside looking in, it seemed as though the appointment of Rose might not deliver the fortunes that had been expected.

The 50-year-old, who accepted the unenviable task of succeeding Andoni Iraola, called for his side to take "responsibility" after the defeat by Chelsea.

"Three points after six games, we need a reaction. Everyone has to take responsibility to do better," said Rose at the time.

"We knew it was going to be a demanding season. We have to stick together and face reality. The reality is we have three points after six games."

The Cherries have not only responded to Rose's rallying cry, they have exceeded all expectations.

Those nine straight wins include five in the league - and his side are now only four points behind second-placed Brighton.

After easing to a 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, Rose said: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game.

"We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."

Bournemouth's nine-game winning streak is a club record - beating two separate runs of eight in 1998-99 and 2012-13

Since arriving in England in July, Rose has come across as a composed presence, regardless of Bournemouth's results.

However, the former Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig manager was unable to hide his delight at his side's record-breaking victory against Forest.

Shortly after the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Rose unleashed a series of celebratory fist pumps in front of the delighted home fans.

It was arguably the first time Rose had let down his guard since arriving on the South Coast four months ago - and who could blame him, given the significance of the result?

It is the first time in the club's history they have won five consecutive Premier League matches.

The prospect of securing European football for a second consecutive season is growing by the week.

In addition to wins over Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Bournemouth have beaten AC Milan in the Europa League and Aston Villa in the League Cup.

Their remarkable run of nine wins across all competitions surpasses their previous record of eight, achieved in both the 1998-99 and 2012-13 seasons.

Bournemouth are currently also second in the Europa League league phase and are one of only three teams to have won all four of their matches so far.

"Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win," Rose told Match of the Day.

Meanwhile, Justin Kluivert - who scored Bournemouth's second goal against Forest - urged his team-mates to remain "humble" and "not settle for less" before upcoming matches against Celta Vigo and Fulham.

'I'll call him' - Justin Kluivert happy he's scored same week as dad Patrick

One of the main reasons behind Bournemouth's upturn in form has been the hot streak forward Evanilson is currently enjoying.

After failing to find the back of the net in his first five appearances of the season, the Brazilian became the first player in club history to score in six consecutive Premier League matches when he broke the deadlock against Forest.

Since joining the Cherries in a club record deal from Porto in August 2024, the 27-year-old has struggled for consistency.

In his first season in England, Evanilson managed 10 goals and five assists in 31 league appearances.

Last season, though, was less productive for the forward, who managed only six goals and three assists in 36 top-flight appearances.

By scoring against Forest, Evanilson has already matched his return from the previous campaign.

"He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest," said Kluivert. "I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team."

It is not only goals that Evanilson is providing for his side this season. He has also proven that he is able to drop between the lines - and out wide - to allow Bournemouth to be a fluid side in transition.

That was evident for the Cherries' second goal against Forest, when Evanilson pulled out to the left touchline and threaded the ball down the line for Marcus Tavernier to cross for the unmarked Kluivert in the centre.

"The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep," added Rose. "The way he scores is quite impressive."

The season has not even reached the halfway point, so no-one at Bournemouth will be getting carried away just yet.

What is possible for the Cherries this term will largely depend on what happens - or, perhaps more importantly, what does not happen - in January.

Bournemouth's impressive recent form - and that of certain individuals - is likely to attract attention from some of the biggest clubs in the Premier League when the transfer window opens in January.

Players such as Evanilson, Rayan, Alex Scott and Junior Kroupi, in particular, are likely to be the subject of interest from elsewhere.

So what should Bournemouth do if some of the Premier League's 'bigger' clubs come knocking for their crown jewels?

Should they resist the premium prices the mid-season market is likely to bring and keep hold of their star quality to preserve their own aspirations this season?

Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart believes the Cherries should try to keep hold of their stars to bolster their own hopes this term - insisting the "sky is the limit" for Rose's side.

"Rather than setting a specific target, like Champions League qualification, they should just enjoy what they are doing," Hart told BBC Sport.

"It is crucial they keep everyone fit and firing, given they have the extra demands of playing in Europe plus the busy Christmas period to come.

"Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott came off the bench today, and that kind of squad depth could be massive for them.

"It is all about keeping themselves in the running because a lot of teams are stumbling right now, whereas Bournemouth are really in a rich vein of form."

#844. ‘Obviously it’s not good’: Arteta sweating over David Raya’s fitness after injury

Keeper close to tears at Newcastle after hurting shoulder

Arsenal held 2-2, with Jaissle hailing ‘excellent’ display

Arsenal were left sweating on the fitness of their goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard was forced off with a shoulder injury during the second half of the 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

It left Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City at the top of the Premier League but Arsenal’s manager was more concerned about Raya following an accidental collision with Newcastle’s William Osula. The Spaniard was helped off in evident pain and looked close to tears.

“Obviously it’s not good David had to come off but at the moment I don’t know [the prognosis],” said Arteta, explaining that a keeper who kept seven clean sheets in the season’s opening 10 games will have the joint scanned on Sunday. “He will have an MRI tomorrow. We will have more information tomorrow. But we know how important David is to us.”

Arsenal were 1-0 up at half-time at St James’ Park thanks to a goal from Eberechi Eze during an opening 45 minutes dominated by the visitors. Newcastle, though, improved significantly after the break and took the lead thanks to goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw before Noni Madueke equalised.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

“My feeling is we have lost two points,” said Arteta. “We were exceptional in the first half but we needed to score three or four goals and we didn’t. We knew there’d be a response but the way we gave Newcastle’s first goal away was completely unacceptable. We came back and scored a second goal but we lacked the moment of magic to kill the game. I don’t think we switched off in the second half; sometimes you have to praise the opposition.”

Matthias Jaissle was left smiling after that second-half performance rescued a game watched by Newcastle’s chair, Yasir al-Rumayyan. He had flown in from Riyadh to witness his first match of the season and is believed to have complimented his head coach afterwards.

“What you saw in the second half was Newcastle’s DNA par excellence and that’s something we can build on,” said Jaissle. “But we’ve got to be humble and realistic. The first half was not good and the second half was excellent. I’ve got mixed feelings because a little more was possible but a point was probably fair.

“I was a bit frustrated at half-time but we encouraged the players to do the high press in the right way and adopt a front-foot approach. There was no hesitating, no doubting, just pure belief and we clicked. I knew we were able to do it, so I was really pleased. We felt unbelievable connections and synergy with the crowd.

“To get a team as good as Arsenal shaking in your stadium was unbelievable. I hope we can carry on this feeling.”

#843. 'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over

Leeds dominate Chelsea for first Stamford Bridge win since 1999

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.

His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.

The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.

Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.

It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.

In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.

It is the first time in 67 years that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.

"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.

"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.

"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."

Okafor double delivers rare win for Leeds at Chelsea

'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?

Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.

Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.

Club record Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.

Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.

After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.

"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.

"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.

"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."

Xabi Alonso post-match interview - Chelsea v Leeds United

Xabi Alonso was appointed Chelsea manager on a four-year deal in May

In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.

They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.

Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.

Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.

The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.

However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.

Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.

Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.

It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.

Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.

Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.

In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.

Chelsea have shown 'no progression' under Alonso - Shearer

Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.

Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.

He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.

Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.

They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.

Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

Likewise, it is almost uncharted territory in Alonso's managerial career, having only previously lost at home by a three-goal margin once.

The stadium emptied and supporters again left early.

Players displayed negative body language and argued with one another both during the match and after the final whistle.

As a result, Alonso has gone from needing to fix defensive issues to dealing with problems that appear to be spreading throughout the squad.

#841. Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return

The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit

There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight.

Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly.

Facing a Birmingham side who arrived top of the table and with firmly held Premier League ambitions, Stoke dominated for an hour, the hitherto goal-shy George Hirst earning a well-deserved lead to send a bumper crowd into raptures. The hand-wringing that then followed Luca Bombino’s sending-off with half an hour remaining made the victory that followed all the sweeter. The 10 men of Stoke were superb. It was no surprise that it took considerable time to convince those in the stands to depart for home after the final whistle.

You see, it is not just that Stoke are second in the table, kept off top spot by goal difference. It is not even that they are undoubtedly the Championship’s form side, with just one defeat in their past 13 games. It is the whole feeling around the place; the resilience Robins has developed, and the belief that they can take on the big guns and beat them.

“We are a work in progress, but today was that step in quality against different opponents. A step up in class,” said Robins. “I thought we were really, really good. The intensity, bravery and the intent that we showed was everything that we asked for.

“And, on the back of that, you’ve got the support that are absolutely right behind us. They trust the players. That is a really good feeling. It’s a great feeling for the players. It’s a heady mix, really.”

Eight years have passed since Stoke were last in the top flight; eight years spent as the Championship equivalent of a sea sponge, doing the bare minimum to survive and letting defeats wash over them while remaining resolutely attached to the rocks of the bottom half of the table. During that time they have ended every campaign no higher than 14th and no lower than 18th. Now, something altogether different is afoot. And this may well be the win that convinces supporters to trust their upbeat instincts.

There was an unavoidable fact heading into Saturday’s game. Stoke’s four defeats this season had all come when tasked with opponents fighting at the top end of the table in Swansea, Southampton, Wolves and Middlesbrough. They had shown themselves capable against much of the division, but a failure to deliver against another Championship heavyweight would have raised legitimate questions about their realistic aspirations.

The three August defeats at the start of the campaign preceded the departure of their best player, Sorba Thomas. His replacement, Jack McGlynn, has been an inspired signing. That this victory came without the talismanic figure of Ethan Galbraith, who was absent through illness, is considerable.

As well as switching to a three-man defence following those season-opening losses, a key factor in their upturn has been the restoration of a touch of old-school Stoke; a physicality that was frequently evident on a cold Saturday afternoon.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Bobby Madley, the referee, did not always take kindly to such an approach – to the indignation of the home crowd, who frequently made their feelings clear – but there was no complaint over Bombino’s sending-off for a second yellow after a rash challenge that left him head in hands before the card had even been shown. Tears followed on his slow trudge towards the tunnel, but he need not have worried, with Birmingham barely threatening thereafter.

Given just five points separate the top eight in the Championship table, it would come as no great shock to see Stoke drop off at some point. They do not have the financial benefit of recent Premier League parachute payments or big-spending owners, they are not prolific goalscorers, and a look at their expected goals and expected points tallies shows them firmly in the bottom half of the table. But they are finding ways to win and if McGlynn has a habit of scoring from unexpectedly long distances, perhaps it is because he is good at it.

Before this weekend, Robins had revealed that a top-eight finish was the pre-season target. “You aim for the stars and hopefully you land trying to grab hold of one,” he had said, rather poetically.

If promotion is a “P” they dare not yet speak of, another one – playoffs – is becoming an increasingly realistic proposition. No more sticking to a rock. Swim free and prosper.

#840. How Grand Theft Auto 6 Already Raced It’s Way Into Red Carpet Fashion

With Grand Theft Auto VI already set to become the biggest game of 2026 after its Nov. 19 launch, model Alex Consani—who lent her voice to the game—showed off her GTA 6-inspired outfit.

Alex Consani is ready for a spin around Vice City.

With the supermodel lending her voice to Grand Theft Auto VI—which is poised to be the biggest video game of the year after making $3.79 billion in preorder and first-day sales, according to parent company Take Two—it was only appropriate that she channel that car vibe into her clutch look for the game’s launch party.

Consani buckled up for the Nov. 18 event at the Gekko restaurant in Miami wearing a short dress from Paris-based label Sevali’s spring 2025 collection that was made out of upcycled seatbelts. The belts crisscrossed around the 23-year-old’s svelte figure, coming to a click—literally—with a buckle that was strapped across her shoulder.

The Victoria’s Secret model completed her look with clear kitten heels and her long blonde hair parted down the middle and flowing behind her.

In the newly released video game, Consani can be heard as a DJ for the in-game radio station Flash FM alongside singer Robyn. The two play songs from the likes of Olivia Rodrigo, Charli XCX, Zara Larsson and more as they put their commentary into high gear.

After playing Rodrigo’s “good 4 u,” Consani can be heard saying in a clip posted from the game, “How do you even fumble a baddie like Olivia?”

She also had some love for Charli XCX, saying, “Whatever Charli XCX does, she’s my medicine. That is my f--king doctor, y’all.”

As for Larsson? After playing the Swedish singer’s hit “Fast Emotion,” Consani commented, “God, I love Zara so much.”

Of course, the model isn’t the only star to lend her voice to GTA VI, with Bad Bunny coming in as host of Latin radio Cocoteo FM, PinkPantheress DJing the indie dance station Stockyard FM, “Weird” Al Yankovic hosting the ’80s station Vice City FM, Morgan Wallen and Lana Del Rey co-hosting Back Country Radio and Rolling Stones guitarist Keith Richards playing his part as DJ Keith on Gloriana Blues Radio.

Grand Theft Auto VI marks the latest installment in the long-running video game series, coming out 13 years after the record-breaking Grand Theft Auto V.

The new game features characters like Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they take part in fan-favorite activities from previous games like car-jackings, shootouts, street-racing, robberies, swimming, jet-skiing, sky-diving, visiting the strip club and, yes, even petting dogs. GTA 6 is set around locations inspired by Floria, allowing players new playable vehicles like kayaks and airboats to roam around the new locale.

#839. Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?

The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

You sign up for a free trial to watch a series after work. A month later, you've forgotten about it. Then you find a charge for your new 12-month subscription on your bank statement. Sound familiar? You're not alone. Now the EU wants to stop that practice.

Under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act (DFA), a company would have to remind you before the free trial ends and get your explicit agreement before it can start charging you. The proposed law would also make it easier to cancel a subscription online and require reminders before certain contracts renew automatically.

The Commission presented the proposal on Wednesday. It wants to give consumers more control over how much time and money they spend online.

"We haven't seen that kind of reform in consumer protection in the last 20 years," Agustin Reyna, director general of the European Consumer Organisation (BEUC), told DW.

His organization pushed for stronger EU rules against manipulative online practices. He sees the proposal as a good starting point for tackling problems that frustrate consumers every day.

The proposal also includes a ban on manipulative marketing tactics, so-called "dark patterns." A concrete example: You are trying to reserve a hotel room and the website claims that only three are left, a potentially false claim to pressure you into buying.

A concert ticket that gets more expensive while you're waiting in an online queue raises a different problem. The price could still go up in the process, but the seller would have to show the current price while you wait and tell you the maximum you could be asked to pay.

Online games that encourage users to spend their money to advance are also targeted. Children would no longer be able to pay to win or get to the next level of their online game.

Marketing and personalized ads would need to be clearly marked and restricted in the case of children. Consumers should get the option to switch off doomscrolling functions such as the autoplay of videos, showing one clip after the other. With these new rules, the EU wants to make apps and websites less addictive.

For Christoph Busch, an academic with a focus on consumer law and digital services based at Osnabrück University in Germany, the option to opt out doesn't go far enough. He argues that a version in which consumers actively have to choose to opt into those functions would be more effective.

"But then there is always the question of proportionality," Busch said. "And I think here the European legislators are trying to balance different interests."

These competing interests are particularly visible in the gaming industry, where interest groups have warned that the proposed EU restrictions could hurt developers and leave players with fewer options to choose from.

Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation called the proposal "unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate," arguing that a ban on selling children features that help them win or advance is worded so broadly that it "could cover almost any purchase in a game."

For Busch, this argument doesn't hold. "If your business model is based on addictive design features, then maybe your business model has to be reviewed," he said.

Catalina Goanta, an associate professor of private law and technology at Utrecht University, emphasized in an interview with DW that "regulation can very easily slide into overregulation."

Even though she believes that the DFA is a solid and reasonable compromise, she argues that prohibiting dark patterns and doomscrolling altogether would be too prohibitive. Many of the issues consumers currently face could be resolved by enforcing existing regulation more effectively, she said.

She points to the fact that the EU has made a name for itself in the past by adding new rules and regulations that have made it more difficult to access the European market, especially for small online businesses.

"Instead of having 27 different regulations to adhere to, companies will now only get one," Reyna said.

For him, this speaks for simplification, especially when the responsibility for compliance is shared between online influencers and the platforms they publish on.

According to the new legislation, the EU would have the possibility to impose fines of up to six percent of a company's global annual revenue should the company violate the law.

The European Parliament and the Council, which represents member state governments, still have to agree on the text and formally adopt it. All experts agree that in that process, changes are still very likely.

"It will be a difficult trialogue, especially in this climate of simplification and deregulation with a focus on strengthening European competitiveness," said Christoph Busch. In that climate, it is not easy to add consumer rights, he adds.

Agustin Reyna is more optimistic. "The parliament is a divided house, much more than in the past," he says. "But consumer protection is a subject that brings parties together because it brings tangible outcomes to people."

#837. Blackburn earn derby draw for Mowbray and extend Burnley’s wait for home win

Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.

In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break. But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn’s first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.

Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have now dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Championship this season.

Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back. Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message “We’re with you, Tony” on the back and the number 900 on the front.

Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray’s absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.

The stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth sustained a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.

The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.

But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a Mowbray-tribute T-shirt from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.

Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley’s lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as Hayden Carter backed off.

The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.

Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker’s leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.

Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.

#835. European football: Barcelona roar back from two goals down to sink Villarreal

Barça prevail 3-2 despite Lamine Yamal’s missed penalty

Atalanta snatch point in thrilling 4-4 draw with Inter

Barcelona came back from two goals behind to beat Villarreal 3-2 at home on Sunday and restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga.

Two goals inside seven minutes from Tajon Buchanan and Tani Oluwaseyi gave Villarreal a commanding lead at Camp Nou and things got worse for Barça when winger Lamine Yamal missed a first-half penalty.

The Catalan giants fought back in style, striking three times in an 11-minute second-half spell to claim victory. Gerard Martín and Fermín López pulled Barça level before Pau Navarro’s own goal gave them victory.

Barça have now won four consecutive matches across all competitions since their Clàsico defeat by Real Madrid in October, and restored their three-point cushion over José Mourinho’s side, who had moved level with Saturday’s victory over Celta Vigo.

Buchanan fired Villarreal ahead in the fifth minute, producing a perfect sliced effort from distance after López gave the ball away. Two minutes later, the visitors doubled their lead through another Canadian, as Oluwaseyi broke down the left flank and smashed an effort into the roof of the net.

Hansi Flick’s side should have pulled one back when Oluwaseyi felled Lamine Yamal in the area and a penalty was given after a VAR review. The teenager took it himself but dragged his spot-kick against the post and wide.

Barcelona came out invigorated for the second half and Peter Gulacsi saved López’s low effort before Martín headed home in the 57th minute from Pedri’s cross.

Four minutes later, López slammed home the second after being teed up by Lamine Yamal and the third was quick to follow. Lamine Yamal’s clever backheel pass fed Eric García, whose cross was bundled into the back of his own net by Navarro, who was later sent off for a second yellow card to complete a miserable afternoon.

Atlético Madrid stayed on the tail of Spain’s top two with a comfortable 3-0 derby win over Getafe.

Diego Simeone’s side are five points behind leaders Barcelona and two off Real Madrid. Álex Baena and Johnny Cardoso’s first-half goals, both set up by Julián Alvarez, got the job done away at the Coliseum stadium in the suburbs south of the Spanish capital.

Álex Grimaldo wrapped up the victory in stoppage time with a penalty, after Getafe’s Djene Dakonam was sent off for fouling Alexander Sørloth.

In Serie A, Atalanta rescued an extraordinary late 4-4 draw against Inter on Sunday as the champions fell three points off the title pace despite Pio Esposito’s hat-trick.

Inter looked comfortable in Bergamo when Petar Sucic’s penalty gave them a two-goal cushion in the 76th minute after Esposito’s goals, but Charles De Ketelaere’s second of the night and a stoppage-time Franck Kessié penalty salvaged a point.

It marked only the third time Inter have dropped points in the league this season, but kept Cristian Chivu’s side in third place, one point behind Roma and three adrift of leaders Lazio.

Esposito struck twice in the first half, pouncing on a deflected ball in the box to sweep home the opener before doubling Inter’s lead by heading home from a corner. Eljif Elmas quickly got one back for the hosts to keep the game alive, but Esposito took his third in composed fashion early in the second half, marking his eighth goal in five games for club and country.

De Ketelaere proved the catalyst for Atalanta’s fightback, pulling a goal back with a header and firing home a powerful finish either side of Sucic’s spot-kick.

That set up a thrilling conclusion as Atalanta chased what had seemed an unlikely point, which they claimed when a penalty was awarded for handball that Kessié calmly converted.

Juventus moved into the top six with a thumping 4-0 victory over Venezia as their recent upturn in form continued. Luciano Spalletti’s side were booed off after a goalless first half, but found four second-half strikes as their unbeaten run stretched to four games in all competitions.

Nick Woltemade sparked the game into life after coming off the bench, pouncing on a loose ball to smash home his second league goal in two games before turning provider for Teun Koopmeiners’ whipped finish. Juan Cabal headed home Juve’s third before Kolo Muani won and converted a penalty to complete the rout, with all four goals coming between the 53rd and 71st minute.

“In the first half, we gave the ball away too much,” Spalletti told Dazn. “It was crucial the players recognised something was missing … in the second half, the players were decisive and more relaxed.”

Milan returned to the top four as Gonçalo Ramos ended his goal drought in a 5-1 thrashing of Frosinone.

Ruben Amorim’s side sealed back-to-back wins for the first time in over a month to go fourth, five points behind leaders Lazio, as club record signing Ramos broke a five-match goalless streak.

Milan got off to a flying start with a Gabriele Calvani own goal and a composed Ramos strike inside 19 minutes. Amorim accused his players of “not helping Ramos” before the game after the Portugal international scored just twice in his first 11 league games following his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

His third was met with a loud roar from the San Siro crowd after he was teed up by Adrien Rabiot, who became the first Milan midfielder since Kaká in 2004 to notch a goal or assist in seven consecutive league games.

The visitors soon hit back through Patrizio Masini, but Milan pulled clear in the second half with some lethal counterattacking as substitutes Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse struck before Christian Pulisic’s dinked finish completed the biggest victory of the Amorim era.

Milutin Osmajic scored twice in a 2-0 win for Genoa at Sassuolo, while Bologna were held to a 1-1 draw by Udinese, who climb off the bottom of the table at Venezia’s expense.

In Ligue 1, Paris FC climbed to second place behind local rivals Paris Saint-Germain with a 4-0 home win over lowly Angers. Patrick Zabi, Luca Koleosho, Maxime Lopez and Diego Coppola all struck in the second half for Liam Rosenior’s high-flying side.

Le Mans struck five minutes into stoppage time to complete a stunning 3-2 comeback ⁠victory at Marseille to move ⁠clear of the ⁠relegation places.

Substitute ​Jean Vercruysse delivered the decisive blow to end Marseille’s run of five successive league victories.

Marseille appeared in complete control ⁠after Amine Gouiri scored for a fourth consecutive game and the Brazilian winger Igor Paixão doubled their lead during a dominant first half.

Louis Mafouta pulled one back with a powerful free-kick 20 ‌minutes from time, although he then had a penalty saved in the 78th minute. Erwan Colas equalised six minutes later before Vercruysse struck late to seal all three points.

Bayern Munich’s Jamal Musiala reportedly suffered another seizure in training this week, according to information received by an AFP subsidiary on Sunday.

Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season with the 23-year-old later revealing he had a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Last Monday’s incident was the second since he made the announcement; the player is reportedly adjusting his medication to properly treat the condition while continuing to play.

News of the incident comes as Bayern have faced criticism from footballers’ union Fifpro over what they claim is a “coordinated campaign” to pressure Musiala to renegotiate the contract he extended in 2025.

On Friday, Bayern’s supervisory board member and former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the Germany international may need to take a pay cut if he cannot recapture his old form.

“Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated,” Rummenigge said. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation … because frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.”

#831. Beverly Hills, 90210 Alum Kimmarie Johnson’s Cause of Death Revealed

Kimmarie Johnson, who appeared on Beverly Hills, 90210 in 1998, died as a result of cardiopulmonary arrest, with ovarian cancer as an underlying cause, per her death certificate.

Authorities have determined what led to Kimmarie Johnson’s death.

Two weeks after the actress, who appeared in Beverly Hills, 90210 and Dude, Where’s My Car?, died Nov. 3 following what her niece described as a “heart event,” her cause of death was determined to be cardiopulmonary arrest, according to a death certificate obtained by People, who listed her age as 59.

While a heart attack—medically referred to as myocardial infarction—is the result of a blocked artery, cardiopulmonary arrest—or cardiac arrest—is when the heart stops beating and is unable to effectively pump blood to the body, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Johnson’s death certificate also listed an underlying cause as metastatic granulosa cell ovarian tumor with peritoneal carcinomatosis, meaning the rare type of ovarian cancer she had spread to her abdominal area, according to the Mayo Clinic.

After her death, Johnson’s niece Rhonda Scott reflected on the joy her aunt brought into the world.

“She radiated a light so strong and bright,” Scott told People in an interview published Nov. 5. “People who came in contact with her felt nothing but positive energy. We will miss her tremendously and will continue to honor her life forever.”

Johnson graduated from Wilkinsburg High School in Pittsburgh in 1985 before studying at California University in Pennsylvania. She won the title of Miss Pennsylvania USA in 1993 and was subsequently a finalist at the Miss USA pageant.

She later moved to New York City and then Los Angeles, where she pursued a career in modeling. While Johnson found small roles on the big screen over the years, she launched her skincare brand SkinGlow by Kimmarie in 2011 and continued to model until her death.

She is survived by her son Cameron Nino, with whom she shared a special connection.

“My [son], u are bright, honest, kind, intelligent, funny and compassionate,” Johnson wrote on Facebook last November alongside a picture of her son for his 22nd birthday. “I’m glad that you enjoyed a good day.”
